- Meeting called to order by Dr. Scune Carrington at 6:30 pm.
- Approval of Minutes of the March 25, 2026, meeting. Motion to approve minutes made by Mr. John Colangeli, seconded by Dr. Scune Carrington. Motion passes 3-0.
- **Introduction and appointment of Drew Crawford as the new Senior Inspector**
  - Mr. Crawford graduated from Hartwick College and immediately entered the field of public health.
  - At the Brookline Department of Health, Mr. Crawford has made a significant impact in his role as Senior Public Health Inspector.
  - He has strengthened public health protections and modernized regulatory operations.
  - In this role, he independently conducted inspections and enforced Massachusetts public health regulations across food safety, housing, environmental health, and water quality systems. He played a key role in interpreting regulatory standards, issuing violations, and coordinating enforcement actions in collaboration with department leadership and town counsel.
  - In addition to enforcement, Mr. Crawford emphasized education and community engagement by investigating complaints, providing technical assistance, and promoting sustainable compliance among residents and businesses.
  - Notably, he designed and implemented an Excel-based inspection and compliance tracking system, which improved scheduling efficiency, documentation accuracy, and regulatory transparency. He also supported the department's transition to enhanced digital records management.
  - Prior to joining Brookline, Mr. Crawford served as a Public Health Specialist with the Saratoga County Department of Health, where he contributed to the county's transition to a full-service health department. His experience included inspections across diverse facilities, environmental health investigations, and regulatory compliance under New York State law.
  - Mr. Crawford remains actively involved in professional organizations, including the Massachusetts Health Officers Association, and holds multiple certifications in food protection, environmental health, and pool operation.
  - Mr. Crawford has been a welcomed addition and has demonstrated an ability to contribute effectively from day one.
  - Motion to appoint Drew Crawford as Senior Inspector made by Mr. John Colangeli, seconded by Dr. Kunwar Singh. Motion passes 3 -0.
- **Introduction and appointment of Tai Nguyen**
  - Mr. Nguyen earned a Bachelor of Science in Public Health from the University of Massachusetts Amherst, followed by a Bachelor of Science in Nursing from the Massachusetts College of Pharmacy and Health Sciences.
  - He began his career as a case manager at Mystic Valley Elder Services, where he supported Vietnamese-speaking older adults with medication management and care navigation.
  - He later served as a Registered Nurse with the Suffolk County Sheriff's Department.
  - Mr. Nguyen then worked for the City of Melrose as a Regional Public Health Nurse, serving multiple communities, including Malden.
  - This role represents a natural transition, as he has already been supporting tuberculosis (TB) case management during the vacancy in the previous Public Health Nurse position.
  - Motion to appoint Tai Nguyen as Public Health Nurse made by Dr. Kunwar Singh seconded by Mr. John Colangeli. Motion passes 3 -0.

## Directors Report

- **Janz Kitchen**
  - Janz Kitchen was visited by Food Inspector Peter Finn on March 26 at that time Mr. Finn left a notice to contact the office that day, Ms. Janz, owner of Janz Kitchen, reached out to Mr. Finn.
  - Mr. Finn explained that he had been contacted by the Massachusetts Department of Public Health Food Protection Program regarding Ms. Janz social media advertisement of apparent food cooked in a home kitchen for sale.
  - Mr. Finn provided Ms. Janz written definition of 590.001(C):FC 1-201.10 (B)

Hi Janz,

Unfortunately, in Malden it is not allowed at all to have a residential kitchen permit, it is forbidden by the zoning ordinance. In order to operate legally, you will need to find a commercial kitchen to operate out of. At that point, it would be basically the normal process to get a Food Service permit. On Thu, Mar 26, 2026 at 4:34 PM JANZfoodTravel Vlog <jclaveria1987@gmail.com> wrote:

On Thu, Mar 26, 2026 at 4:29 PM Peter Finn <pfinn@cityofmalden.org> wrote:

Good afternoon Janz,

Thank you for getting back to me. I am a Health Inspector for the City of Malden Inspectional Services Department. I was contacted by the Massachusetts Department of Public Health Food Protection Program regarding your social media advertisements for Janz Kitchen, which appears to offer food cooked in your home kitchen for sale. This activity is not legal under 105.CMR 590.000 State Sanitary Code, Chapter X – Minimum Sanitation Standards for Food Establishments.

The specific code violations are as follows:

- 590.001(C); FC 1-201.10(B) Terms Defined: Food Establishment.
  - (1) Food establishment means an operation that:
    - (a) stores, prepares, packages, serves, vends food directly to the consumer, or otherwise provides food for human consumption such as a restaurant; satellite or catered feeding location; catering operation if the operation provides food directly to a consumer or to a conveyance used to transport people not including farm trucks; market; vending location; conveyance used to transport people; institution; food bank; and,
    - (b) relinquishes possession of food to a consumer directly, or indirectly through a delivery service such as home delivery of grocery orders or restaurant takeout orders, or delivery service that is provided by common carriers.
  - (2) Food establishment includes:
    - (a) An element of the operation such as a transportation vehicle or a central preparation facility that supplies a vending location or satellite feeding location unless the vending or feeding location is permitted by the regulatory authority; and
    - (b) An operation that is conducted in a mobile, stationary, temporary, or permanent facility or location; where consumption is on or off the premises; and regardless of whether there is a charge for the food.
- 590.003; FC 3-201.11 (B) Compliance with Food Law: Food prepared in a private home may not be used or offered for human consumption in a food establishment.
- 590.006; FC 6-202.111 Private Homes and Living or Sleeping Quarters, Use Prohibition: A private home, a room used as living or sleeping quarters, or an area directly opening into a room used as living or sleeping quarters may not be used for conducting food establishment operations.
- 590.008; FC 8-301.11 Prerequisite for Operation: A person may not operate a food establishment without a valid permit to operate issued by the regulatory authority.

Additionally, Malden City Code 12.28.030(C) prohibits all commercial food preparation in residences.

**Therefore, you must:**

- Immediately cease and desist from any food establishment activity without a permit.
- Immediately cease and desist from any food establishment activity in a private home.

Please let me know if you have any questions regarding this correspondence.

Thank you,
Peter Finn

Health Inspector
